        Quick facts

        Facts checked Oct. 31, 2026
        Motors and speed
        Unlimited horsepower; 40 mph by day. Idle speed within 100 ft of shore and bridges. Boats 22 ft or shorter, no personal watercraft.
        Ramps and access
        Home Road ramp and marina, and the Bellepoint ramp. Canoe and kayak launches at Twin Lakes and on the east side.
        Docks, checked Nov. 3, 2026: The city lists the marina dock season as May 1 to Oct. 31, so the marina docks are done for 2026. No date posted yet for pulling the ramp docks. Source: Columbus Recreation and Parks, Marinas & Docks. Dock season, all lakes.
        Normal pool
        Full pool is the City dam crest, 848.5 ft. ODNR fishing map depths are based on 847.9 ft. Live level: USGS gauge 03220500.
        Night rules
        10 mph from sunset to sunrise (City code). City park hours are 7 a.m. to 11 p.m.; check posted signs before a night trip. Source: Columbus Recreation and Parks, O’Shaughnessy Reservoir.

        Sources: Columbus Recreation and Parks, O’Shaughnessy Reservoir; Columbus City Code 921.01-1(G); ODNR, O’Shaughnessy Reservoir Fishing Area.

        How to read this
        • Pool is lake surface elevation (ft NGVD29), not the depth of any hole or channel.
        • Full pool here is the City of Columbus dam crest, 848.5 ft. The ODNR fishing map’s depths are based on 847.9 ft, so contours are off by about (847.9 − pool). If pool is lower, real water is shallower than printed.
        • No public water temp gauge: the USGS gauge at the dam reads level only, and the City says its reservoir temperatures are not monitored. The temp slot says n/a. Nothing is estimated.
        • USGS values are provisional (param 62614) and can be revised. USGS-03220500.
        • City of Columbus drinking-water reservoir: unlimited horsepower, 40 mph by day and 10 mph from sunset to sunrise, boats 22 ft or shorter, no personal watercraft, tubing or swimming, and idle speed within 100 ft of shore and bridges (City of Columbus).

        Tonight’s bite

        A rule of thumb guide, not a promise.

        How the bite is rated

        The Bite is this site’s own rule of thumb, not fishing science and not a forecast. It adds points from readings already on this page.

        • Barometer, the change over the last 3 hours at the lake’s NWS station. Falling slowly +2, steady +1, rising slowly 0, falling fast 0, rising fast −1. Steady means within 0.02 inHg; fast means 0.06 inHg or more.
        • Wind, tonight’s average NWS hourly speed from sunset to 2 AM (the top of each hour’s range). Under 3 mph 0, 3 to 12 mph +1, 13 to 18 mph 0, over 18 mph −2.
        • Moon, worked out on this phone. New or full moon tonight (or under 10% or over 90% lit) +1, otherwise 0.
        • Water temp, from this lake’s USGS gauge where one reports it. 55 to 80°F +1, colder than 45 or warmer than 86°F −1, anything between 0. It never makes a rating alone.
        • Thunder anywhere in tonight’s NWS forecast makes it Tough, whatever the points.

        4 points or more is Good, 2 or 3 is Fair, less is Tough. A missing reading counts 0, and with no barometer trend and no wind there is no rating.

              What this site is

              • Unofficial Ohio fishing hub with night-dock atmosphere: Hoover, Alum Creek, Buckeye Lake, O’Shaughnessy, Griggs, Indian Lake, Delaware Lake, Deer Creek Lake, Madison Lake, Knox Lake, Clear Fork Reservoir, Seneca Lake, Dillon Lake, Lake Logan, Salt Fork Lake, Burr Oak Lake, Dow Lake, Mosquito Creek Lake, Berlin Lake, West Branch Reservoir, Pymatuning Lake, Lake Milton and Leesville Lake
              • Species pages with limit reminders from the ODNR 2026–27 rules
              • One example log entry, marked Example · not ODNR / City / USGS
              Night fishing can be dangerous in storms, heat, and low visibility. Wear a life jacket when it calls for it. 40 mph, 10 mph after sunset · idle within 100 ft of shore · drinking-water reservoir · license ages 16+. See About.
